info.title: Duffel Flights API
info.description: Flight search, booking, changes, and cancellations through the Duffel network. Search by route and passengers, refresh offers before ordering, then book with a balance payment. Orders are real bookings with real airlines: the Create Order call settles the actual fare plus a service fee through your AIsa balance, so verify slices and passenger details before confirming.

destination.description: IATA airport code (ATL) or city code

type.description: Use for adults; passengers under 18 must provide age instead

id.description: Passenger id from the offer request response

email.description: Must be the passenger's own email

infant_passenger_id.description: Infant passenger id this adult is responsible for; one infant per adult

amount.description: Must equal the refreshed offer total_amount

currency.description: Must equal the refreshed offer total_currency

refund_amount.description: 0.00 when non-refundable; null when the airline has not quoted

post.description: Search flights by route and passengers. Returns an offer request with priced offers including full segment details. $0.02 per request.

max_connections.description: Maximum connections per slice; 0 for direct flights only

get.description: Retrieve a single offer request by id. $0.005 per request.
List your offer requests, newest first. $0.005 per request.
Refresh a single offer. Call immediately before ordering: the returned price and expiry are authoritative, and offers expire. $0.005 per request.

404.description: Offer not found or expired; search again

get.description: List flight offers for a specific offer request. Pass the offer_request_id returned when creating or retrieving an offer request. $0.005 per request.

parameters.name: offer_request_id
parameters.description: The offer request id whose flight offers should be listed.

get.description: Seat map per segment for an offer. Not supported by every airline. Seats can only be selected when creating the order via services. $0.005 per request.

post.description: Book the selected offer and pay with your Aisa balance. The payment amount must equal the refreshed offer total; the settled charge is the fare plus a small service fee. This creates a real booking with the airline and issues a real electronic ticket. Returns the airline booking reference and ticket documents. Always refresh the offer immediately before ordering, and verify passenger details — post-booking change and refund rules follow the airline's fare conditions.

services.description: Optional ancillaries (bags, seats) by service id

422.description: Validation error, expired offer, or amount mismatch (not charged)

post.description: Hold the selected order without immediate payment. Same body as Create Flight Order plus "type": "hold" in data. Unpaid orders expose payment_required_by and intended_payment_methods.
Fetch change offers for a paid order. The response embeds order_change_offers with new_total_amount, penalty_total_amount, and change_total_amount. New slices must keep the original cabin class.

201.description: Change request with embedded change offers

get.description: Retrieve a change request with its change offers. $0.005 per request.

post.description: Execute a selected change offer. The price difference settles through your Aisa balance.
Fetch the refund quote for an order. refund_amount may be 0.00 (non-refundable) or null (airline has not quoted). Only the most recently created cancellation can be confirmed.

get.description: Retrieve a cancellation quote by id. $0.005 per request.

post.description: Confirm the most recent cancellation quote for an order. The refund is issued to the payment source.

get.description: Retrieve a flight order by its ID, including its slices, passengers, payment status, and documents. $0.005 per request.

data.description: An order represents a booking with an airline

airline_initiated_changes.description: The airline-initiated changes for this Order

action_taken.description:
The action taken in response to this airline-initiated change.

Accepted, cancelled and changed reflect your action in accepting the change,
cancelling the order or changing the order respectively.

action_taken_at.description: The [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) datetime at which an action was taken

added.description: List of updated [slices and segments](/docs/api/orders/schema#orders-schema-slices) following the change. These slices and segments may each have a new ID as a result of the changes.

conditions.description:
The conditions associated with this slice, describing the kinds of modifications you can make and any penalties that will apply to those modifications.
This condition is applied only to this slice and to all the passengers associated with this order - for information at the order level (e.g. "what happens if I want to change all the slices?") refer to the `conditions` at the top level.
If a particular kind of modification is allowed, you may not always be able to take action through the Duffel API. In some cases, you may need to contact the Duffel support team or the airline directly.

change_before_departure.description:
Whether this slice can be changed before the departure.
If the slice can be changed for all of the passengers then the `allowed` property will be `true` and information will be provided about any penalties.
If none of the passengers on the slice can be changed then the `allowed` property will be `false`.
In all other cases this property will be `null` indicating we can't provide the information for this slice.
The `penalty_amount` is specific to changing this slice and may not be the penalties that is applied if the entire order is changed.

allowed.description: Whether this kind of modification is allowed post-booking

penalty_amount.description:
If the modification is `allowed` then this is the amount payable to apply the modification to all passengers. If there is no penalty, the value will be zero.
If the modification isn't `allowed` or the penalty is not known then this field will be `null`.
If this is `null` then the `penalty_currency` will also be `null`.

penalty_currency.description:
The currency of the `penalty_amount` as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code.
This will be in a currency determined by the airline, which is not necessarily the same as the currency of the offer or order.
If this is `null` then `penalty_amount` will also be `null`.

conditions.description:
The conditions associated with this order, describing the kinds of modifications you can make to it and any penalties that will apply to those modifications.
This information assumes the condition is applied to all of the slices and passengers associated with this order - for information at the slice level (e.g. "what happens if I just want to change the first slice?") refer to the `slices`.
If a particular kind of modification is allowed, you may not always be able to take action through the Duffel API. In some cases, you may need to contact the Duffel support team or the airline directly.

change_before_departure.description:
Whether the whole order can be changed before the departure of the first slice.
If all of the slices on the order can be changed then the `allowed` property will be `true`. Refer to the `slices` for information about change penalties.
If any of the slices on the order can't be changed then the `allowed` property will be `false`. In this case you should refer to the `slices` conditions to determine if any part of the order is changeable.
If the airline hasn't provided any information about whether this order can be changed then this property will be `null`.

allowed.description: Whether this kind of modification is allowed post-booking

penalty_amount.description:
If the modification is `allowed` then this is the amount payable to apply the modification to all passengers. If there is no penalty, the value will be zero.
If the modification isn't `allowed` or the penalty is not known then this field will be `null`.
If this is `null` then the `penalty_currency` will also be `null`.

penalty_currency.description:
The currency of the `penalty_amount` as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code.
This will be in a currency determined by the airline, which is not necessarily the same as the currency of the offer or order.
If this is `null` then `penalty_amount` will also be `null`.

refund_before_departure.description:
Whether the whole order can be refunded before the departure of the first slice.
If all of the slices on the order can be refunded then the `allowed` property will be `true` and information will be provided about any penalties.
If any of the slices on the order can't be refunded then the `allowed` property will be `false`.
If the airline hasn't provided any information about whether this order can be refunded then this property will be `null`.

synced_at.description:
Airlines are always the source of truth for orders. The orders returned in the Duffel API are a view of those orders.
This field is the [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) datetime at which the order was last synced with the airline.
If this datetime is in the last minute you can consider the order up to date.

tax_amount.description: The amount of tax payable on the order for all the flights booked

tax_breakdown.description:
The airline's breakdown of `tax_amount` by tax code.
The list is empty when the airline gives us no usable itemisation. Treat an empty list as "no breakdown available" rather than "no tax".
Each line is in the currency the airline quoted it in, which is given per line. Where Duffel converts the price into your billing currency, that currency differs from `tax_currency`, so the lines cannot be compared with `tax_amount` without converting them.
Even in a single currency, the lines can add up to less than `tax_amount`: a line the airline quoted without a code, a currency or an amount is dropped, and some airlines itemise only part of the tax they charge. Do not reconcile against it, and do not use it to compute a total.
A line's `name` is the short label for the charge and its `description` the fuller explanation of what it is and who levies it.
A line's `name`, `description` and `carrier_imposed` are all nullable, and are `null` for a tax code we cannot yet classify.

amount.description:
The amount charged under this code, for all passengers.
A refundable tax appears as a negative amount.

carrier_imposed.description:
Whether the charge is set by the airline itself, rather than by a government or an airport.
This is `null` for a code we cannot classify. Do not read `null` as `false`.

code.description:
The tax code the airline used for this charge, as it was quoted to us.
Codes are mostly the IATA ticket tax codes (for example `GB` for UK Air Passenger Duty), but an airline is free to quote a code that is not in that list.

currency.description:
The currency of the `amount`, as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code.
This is the currency the airline quoted the tax in. Where Duffel converts the price into your billing currency, it will differ from `tax_currency`.

description.description:
A plain-English description of what the charge is for, written by Duffel.
This is `null` for a code we do not yet have a description for. It is never the airline's own wording.
description.example: UK Air Passenger Duty, an excise duty charged on each passenger departing from a UK airport, banded by distance and cabin.

name.description:
A short label for the charge, written by Duffel: the country that levies it (or the airline, for a charge the airline sets itself) followed by the charge.
Use it where a line item has to fit beside its amount. This is `null` for a code we do not yet have a name for. It is never the airline's own wording.

tax_currency.description:
The currency of the `tax_amount`, as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code.
It will match your organisation's billing currency unless you’re using Duffel as an accredited IATA agent, in which case it will be in the currency provided by the airline (which will usually be based on the country where your IATA agency is registered).

total_amount.description: The total price of the order for all the flights and services booked, including taxes

total_currency.description:
The currency of the `total_amount`, as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code.
It will match your organisation's billing currency, with two exceptions. If the order was paid using a card or airline credit, it will be the currency the airline charged in, even if the offer you booked showed your billing currency. If you’re using Duffel as an accredited IATA agent, it will be the currency provided by the airline (usually based on the country where your IATA agency is registered).

void_window_ends_at.description:
Some paid orders are eligible to be voided, typically within the first 24 hours after payment. An order that is cancelled within this window is eligible for a full refund.
Note that orders created near to the initial departure date i.e. within 7 days may not be eligible for void.
This field is the [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) datetime at which the shall no longer be eligible to be void, after which any refunds shall be subject to the conditions on the order.
